title: No commit-completeness rubric criterion exists for canonical skill runs
description: The rubric system has no criterion verifying that the working tree is clean (no uncommitted files) before the candidate tag is created. Loose files after Phase 7's git_commit go undetected until post-run manual review. The existing tool-errors criterion covers ToolHandler failures but not incomplete staging. The clean-working-tree condition is objectively verifiable at the shell level and should not depend on the agent or reviewer noticing the gap.
proposed_resolution: Add a kernel-authoritative clean-working-tree criterion to the run command baseline rubrics (run.rubrics.md), injected by verify_rubrics from git status --porcelain output after the agent loop completes — following the same pattern as tool-errors. A non-empty porcelain output is a Fail. Alternatively, add a posttooluse hook on git_commit that runs git status --porcelain and emits a warning signal if output is non-empty. Either approach catches the loose-files class of error without relying on agent or reviewer observation.
